item.question: Angles are classified in three groups as shown (a box with three columns of angle drawings). Right angles are shown in the second group. What could be the common feature of the other two groups?
steps: Compare each group's angles with an L-shaped right angle.
Left group is smaller than a right angle; right group is bigger but under a straight angle.
item.answer: First group: all angles are less than a right angle (less than a quarter turn), called acute angles. Third group: all angles are greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle (more than a quarter turn, less than a half turn), called obtuse angles.

item.question: Write the measures of the following angles: a. ∠KAL b. ∠WAL c. ∠TAK. (Worked in the book for a: the vertex coincides with the centre of the protractor, so the number of units of 1 degree between KA and AL gives ∠KAL = 30°. Follow-up: Making use of the medium sized and large sized marks, is it possible to count the number of units in 5s or 10s?) a) ∠KAL b) ∠WAL c) ∠TAK
steps_tex: The vertex $A$ is at the centre of the protractor, so the units of $1$ degree between two arms give the angle.
The long marks come every $10\text{ units}$ and the medium marks $5\text{ units}$ after each long mark, so we can count in $10s$ or in $5s$.
$\angle KAL$ holds $3$ long steps: $3 \times 10^\circ = 30^\circ$.
$\angle WAL$ holds $5$ long steps: $5 \times 10^\circ = 50^\circ$.
$\angle TAK$ holds $12$ long steps: $12 \times 10^\circ = 120^\circ$.
Check by counting in $5s$: $6 \times 5^\circ = 30^\circ$, $10 \times 5^\circ = 50^\circ$ and $24 \times 5^\circ = 120^\circ$, the same as the counts in $10s$.
item.answer_tex: $(a)$: $\angle KAL = 30^\circ$, $(b)$: $\angle WAL = 50^\circ$, $(c)$: $\angle TAK = 120^\circ$. Yes, it is possible to count in $5s$ or $10s$.
